newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden says it unaffected by Finnish ERM move.
newsitem.headline: Sweden says it unaffected by Finnish ERM move.

text.p: Sweden said on Saturday that Finland's membership of the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) did not affect its wait-and-see stance.

"ERM membership is not on the current agenda. Sweden has good chances of meeting the criteria for EMU membership. Membership of the exchange rate mechanism demands a period of stability in the Swedish economy.
"In addition there has to be broad support in society for linking the crown to the ERM," deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten said in a statement.

Finance Minister Erik Asbrink also said Finland's adhesion to the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) did not affect Sweden, and added that there was no reason to change Sweden's monetary and currency policies.
Asbrink said in a statement that Sweden and Finland had taken their own positions on the question of ERM and EMU.
"Finland's decision to adhere to the ERM does not affect Sweden's view. It is the government's view that it is not on the agenda for Sweden to link the crown to the ERM," he added.
"Price stability is the overwhelming goal of monetary policy. This direction for monetary and currency policy has been successful and there is no reason to change it," he said.

The EU monetary committee agreed on Saturday to allow the Finnish markka to join the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) currency grid at a central rate of 3.04 to the German mark, the committee said in a statement.
Entry into the ERM is viewed as a step towards Finland joining the future EU single currency when it is launched at the start of 1999.
Sweden's ruling Social Democratic Party has said it will decide at a congress next year if it is to link the crown to the exchange rate mechanism or seek to join EMU.

Opinion polls show public opinion is against Sweden linking its currency to the exchange rate mechanism and Prime Minister Goran Persson, a personal supporter of monetary union, is seeking a public debate on membership.

"In recent years imbalances in the Swedish economy have been reduced and state finances have improved rapidly. Sweden's credibility as a low-inflation country is in the process of being established," Heikensten added.
